transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (Lyon Biotech), Omar Reid (Platform Eng), Luc Moreau (CTO)

Summary (auto-gen):
- Align on POC scope: clinical QA assistant for multi-lingual notes (EN/FR/ES), low hallucination, regulatory data controls.
- Agree to run benchmark on two open models (Llama3-70B, Mistral-2-34B) with 3 quantization profiles.
- Target: 95% top-1 factual accuracy on curated evals, hallucination <2% on closed-domain tests, 90th pct latency <300ms on a dedicated 8-GPU pool.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Maya: yeah, loud and clear. thanks.
[00:05] Sofia: great. quick intros, i'm sofia, AE at Redwood, and diego here is our systems SE who will run the benchmarks, diego do you want to say hi?
[00:12] Diego: hi all, diego martinez, infra and benchmarking, i'll own the config and run the tests with lyon's samples.
[00:18] Luc: luc moreau, cto, i'll be listening for infra / compliance stuff.
[00:22] Omar: omar, platform eng, i'll handle networking and keys.
[00:25] Maya: maya, head of ml, i'll own success criteria and eval sets.

[00:30] Sofia: cool, so high level, you sent over the product brief - multilingual clinical QA, right? we're scoping a POC to validate quality and perf on open models and decide between hosted vs dedicated vs private. correct?
[00:41] Maya: yes that's right. we want open models to avoid vendor lock and control costs, but we need clinical-level accuracy and data residency. also french and spanish support are mandatory.

[00:54] Diego: quick clarifying q - what's your target latency for interactive QA? and expected concurrency?
[00:58] Maya: target is snappy, our UX wants sub-300ms 90th pct for answer token generation on interactive queries. concurrency initially is small, maybe 10-20 concurrent users, but peak could be 100+ in a day for batch jobs. sessions average 350 tokens returned, prompts ~150 tokens.
[01:14] Omar: also cost is a factor; we can't exceed roughly $0.0008 per output token on POC if possible.

[01:20] Sofia: awesome, those are good constraints. for success criteria we typically split into: quality (accuracy and hallucination), latency/throughput, and security/compliance. you mentioned hallucination limits; do you have a metric or threshold?
[01:33] Maya: ideally hallucination under 2% on our closed-domain set. accuracy - we'd like 95% top-1 on curated clinical Q/A. tolerance for tradeoffs if latency is good but quality suffers is low.

[01:45] Diego: ok makes sense. on models, to start we recommend a short list: Llama3-70B (quantized), Mistral-2-34B-instruct, and a smaller 13B instruct family as a baseline for cost comparisons. we can also try an LLM specialized for biomedical — there's a community fine-tuned variant we've seen but need to validate license.
[02:05] Maya: do those handle french/spanish well out of box?
[02:07] Diego: Mistral-2 shows good multilingual generalization, Llama3-70B also, especially with instruction-tuning. smaller 13B will be weaker in FR/ES. fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation will help both.

[02:20] Luc: what about hallucinations and groundedness? we need citations or at least references returned where possible.
[02:25] Sofia: we discussed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) as a mitigation, combined with conservative decoding and filtering. Redwood supports prefix cache, RAG connectors, and you can pin a model variant and fallback to a smaller/safer model for high-risk queries.

[02:40] Omar: networking / security — for POC we prefer dedicated capacity in our cloud account or a private deployment? what's the typical path?
[02:45] Diego: two flows: quickest is Redwood hosted with dedicated tenancy (reserved pool) and customer VPC peering for data egress controls; the other is private (control plane in your VPC) which takes longer but meets stricter compliance. for POC we suggest dedicated pool in Redwood with KMS-integration and audit logs turned on.

[02:58] Maya: timeline? we want results fast, ideally benchmarks in two weeks.
[03:02] Sofia: totally doable. plan: you provide data in 2 business days, we spin up benchmark env and run tests over 3 configs (float16, 4-bit quant, 8-bit quant) across the two models, and deliver results in ~7 days. so roughly 10 business days from today.

[03:18] Diego: benchmark metrics we'll capture: p95 latency (token and request), 90th token latency, throughput (rps), GPU util, and qualitative metrics: accuracy on your evals, hallucination rate, and cost per token.

[03:33] Maya: can you explain the quantization tradeoffs briefly? we saw 4-bit can save costs but hurts quality sometimes.
[03:37] Diego: yes, 4-bit and quantized kernels reduce GPU memory and improve throughput but can slightly degrade generation fidelity, especially for complex medical reasoning. for Llama3-70B we expect small drop in factuality at 4-bit vs fp16; 8-bit often is a good middle ground. we'll report Rouge/F1 and confusion on critical entity extraction.

[03:55] Sofia: also we'll measure hallucination proxies — like hallucination on closed-book QA where answers should be exact, and a span-extraction check for entity hallucination.

[04:05] Luc: what about multilingual evals? we have ~1k French Q/A, 800 Spanish, rest english.
[04:09] Maya: yes, we'll provide those. please also run zero-shot vs few-shot prompts.

[04:15] Diego: noted. specifically we'll run: 1) english baseline, 2) french zero-shot, 3) spanish zero-shot, 4) french few-shot (3 exemplars), 5) same for spanish.

[04:27] Omar: about logging and data retention — we need conversation logs to be disabled by default and storage within EMEA. is that feasible for dedicated pool?
[04:34] Diego: yes dedicated and private both support customer-managed S3 and region pinning. we can disable retention and ensure KMS keys are customer-managed. we'll capture audit logs for the control plane but you can limit payload persistence.

[04:47] Maya: benchmarks — what about synthetic load? we want to simulate 50 concurrent sessions with bursts to 120.
[04:53] Diego: we'll create synthetic load harness matching your tokens/session numbers and run a throughput sweep to identify sweet spot for batch size / concurrency. we'll also measure tail latency under burst.

[05:04] Sofia: on model shortlist, i'll propose we standardize on the two primary axes: quality-first (Llama3-70B fp16 / 8-bit) and cost-first (Mistral-2-34B quantized). and include a 13B baseline to set expectations. you okay with that?
[05:16] Maya: yes that sounds reasonable. if the Llama3 variant meets hallucination and latency targets we can pursue dedicated deployment; otherwise we may prefer aggressive RAG with Mistral if it's cheaper.

[05:28] Luc: licensing question — any constraints on using community fine-tune models in regulated environment?
[05:32] Sofia: depends on license; many community fine-tunes are MIT/BSD-like but some have restrictions. we'll flag any license risk and prefer models with compatible licenses or use your private fine-tune under contract.

[05:44] Omar: are there specific infra minimums you need for the dedicated 8-GPU pool?
[05:48] Diego: for Llama3-70B quantized we'd recommend A100/H100 class hardware; 8x80GB GPUs for comfortable KV cache and throughput; for Mistral-2-34B 4x80GB or 8x40GB can work. we'll size exact GPU types after the first benchmark run.

[06:04] Maya: success criteria recap — 95% accuracy, hallucination <2%, 90th token latency <300ms, cost per output token < $0.0008 on POC. also FR/ES parity within 5% of EN performance.

[06:18] Sofia: got it. we'll codify those in the benchmark plan.

[06:22] Diego: any other blockers?
[06:24] Omar: network peering takes time; i'll start the request today. also we need an NDA around dataset sharing.
[06:30] Maya: we'll redact PHI for the POC datasets but it's still sensitive.

[06:34] Sofia: understood — we'll send our standard DPA + benchmarking NDA with instructions for S3 upload.

[06:38] Luc: ok timeline wise, when's follow-up?
[06:40] Sofia: we'll target a benchmark kickoff 2026-10-08 and results 2026-10-15, then follow-up deep-dive the week after to review.

[06:48] Maya: works for us. thanks.
[06:50] Sofia: sweet, we'll recap next steps in email. thanks everyone.

Close notes:
- Agreed models: Llama3-70B (quality-first), Mistral-2-34B-instruct (cost-first), 13B instruct baseline.
- Benchmark configs: fp16, 8-bit, 4-bit quant; multilingual zero/few-shot tests; RAG experiments to be scheduled if initial quality low.
- Security: dedicated pool with customer KMS, EMEA region pinning, retention controls.
